Source: Linux dwarfort, ELF:bcc6789e6fb477b785a2b02be80b8b1b054ff88c.
This directory contains offline native source extraction, not game execution
or a translation test. Addresses belong to this ELF, not the historical PE.

Native sign creation
  Owner: 0xfa3400..0xfcd78b (site construction).
  The complete owner instructions, literal operands, conditional edges and
  compiler switch entries are retained in elf-*.asm and elf-*.tsv.
  Relevant region: entry 0xfc9297, continuation 0xfbdd56.
  sign-fragment-ranges.tsv and sign-fragment-edges.tsv preserve its entire
  reachable control flow, including the 18-target switch at 0xfc9404.
  sign-fragment-decompiled.c is Ghidra's decompilation of this region.
  The region boundaries are only an offline analysis device; they are not
  original function boundaries and do not modify the game's machine code.
  The continuation is replaced by RET only in the disposable Ghidra memory
  database so the decompiler cannot absorb unrelated construction code.

  The new item_slabst stores the original inscription at +0xe0 and its
  engraving subtype at +0x104 in this Linux ABI. No new random name is chosen
  by the display writer or by the translator.

  Shop branch (building type other than the abstract tavern case):
    info = site_realization_building.info (+0x58)
    if info.name.has_name (+0x82):
      stored_writing = EnglishName(info.name +0x10, English=true,
                                   first_person=false) + " / "
    switch info.type (+0x08), values 0..17:
      append the corresponding literal from sign-text-branches.tsv
      set the corresponding slab subtype (7..24)
    default:
      append no category and keep the default slab subtype (-1)
      an existing named prefix still translates through the {p} / production
      (market-only shop selectors 18..24 do not acquire invented sign text)

  Tavern branch (building type 0x16):
    resolve the abstract building via its stored ID (+0x4c)
    call virtual getName at +0x10 if the lookup supplies an object
    if name exists and name.has_name (+0x72):
      stored_writing = EnglishName(name, true, false) + " / "
    append "Tavern"; set subtype 25
    missing object, null name and has_name=false all use bare "Tavern"

  All 18 shop literals and the tavern literal have both bare and named
  inscription productions. Their native selectors, subtype, title, source
  strings and category translations are recorded in sign-text-branches.tsv.

Stored name production
  0x12c58d0..0x12c6e5c formats the complete language_name, respecting its
  first_name/nickname visibility policy and seven WORD/POS component slots.
  It supplies front/rear compounds, up to two adjectives, a hyphenated
  compound, TheX and OfX groups. "The ", "the ", "Of ", "of ", spaces,
  nickname delimiters and the hyphen belong to this formatter.
  Shop and tavern sign calls pass English=true, first_person=false.
  0x1cc3980..0x1cc3ac7 selects all nine English POS forms (0..8); an invalid
  word index or POS emits no word. English fields come from the installed
  language_words.txt, retained in name/raw-WORD-forms.tsv.
  Capitalization is the imported capitalize_string_words at PLT 0x424200;
  0x69f9b0 is std::string mutation, with no separate name vocabulary.
  name/elf-decompiled.c retains Ghidra's formatter and selector pseudocode;
  name/elf-*.tsv retain all native conditions, branch edges and POS targets.
  Existing procedural/name vocabulary and the complete generated-name
  compositor handle these dynamic names; whole randomized names are not
  reduced to a finite list of screenshot-specific replacements.

Item detail consumer
  0xe76ce0..0xe7c9a8 is the shared item description writer.
  For a slab with an empty saved inscription it appends no writing sentence.
  Its readable branch copies the saved string between 'The slab reads "'
  (0xe777fe) and '".' (0xe7782a).
  Adventure literacy selects the existing 'There is writing on the slab,
  but you cannot read.' production. Color/reading markup is a separate
  display concern and does not become part of the inscription grammar.
  Slab title owner: 0xe6d5b0..0xe6d7d3. Shared noun: 0x12b6a70..0x12bdd2f.
  elf-item-decompiled.c contains these three complete item/text functions.
  The site-construction owner is retained as full original instructions,
  with its relevant sign region decompiled separately to avoid absorbing
  unrelated world-generation and map-placement logic.
  Subtype 0 uses memorial; 7..24 use the 18 shop titles; 25 uses tavern sign;
  all other values use slab. The shared noun supplies the plural 's'.
  Memorial identification, secrets (6), true-name slabs (26), quality,
  improvements, contamination, wear and item location retain their existing
  typed item/slab and memorial handlers.

Translation data
  data/runtime/item-description-translations.tsv owns 38 category sentence
  productions: one complete {p} name followed by each exact native suffix,
  and the bare category form, plus the named default branch. The {p} field uses the existing generated-name
  compositor; the outer quoted {q} field uses the existing item prose parser.
  Matching scoped hH/hHt rows are written directly to translations.tsv so
  a data-only change needs neither a generator nor a core build.
  These are item-description rules, not global substring replacements.
  The slab TOML and flat noun entries also correct cloth shop sign(s) from
  clothing to cloth. Existing user changes and squad.alias rules are kept.
